answer_1.quote: ...We develop rigorous annotation guidelines for identifying full and partial hallucinations and omissions and use these guidelines for manual annotation of translations in all 18 directions...
answer_1.outputs: translations with sentence-level and token-level hallucination and omission annotations

answer_2.quote: ...We used some methods from: ChrF++, reference-based COMET and referenceless COMET‑QE, and Seq‑Logprob ... We also used some methods introduced in: cosine similarity coming from LASER3 and LaBSE, a bidirectional XNLI score, and ALTI+ source contributions...

answer_4.quote: ...To ensure annotation quality, guidelines and qualification tests were prepared by professional linguists. For annotation, we choose professional translators (2 for each language) who are allowed to annotate our data only after passing a specifically developed qualification test...
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were instructed to mark hallucinations, omissions, severity levels, and whether the translation is incomprehensible (garbled or in another language).
